source.title: Global Optimality Beyond Two Layers: Training Deep ReLU Networks via Convex Programs

record.file_problem: Whole paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests training outcomes on some claim-relevant settings using a three-layer parallel ReLU architecture, SGD, and an approximate convex formulation, but its CIFAR-10 result is only shown in accuracy plots and the benchmark recipe differs from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training/test accuracy curves for its network and the proposed convex formulation, and explicit SGD outcomes on a synthetic regression problem. The synthetic results bear on whether SGD reaches a global minimum as subnetworks increase. Figure 5 does not provide textual numeric values for training accuracy; the study's stated comparison is that the convex formulation provides a performance boost. UCI results are regression objectives, not classification error, and do not directly test the listed versions. Citations and discussion of other studies are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study reports related optimization results, but none tests a listed version. Its CIFAR-10 architecture is a parallel fully connected ReLU network, whereas V1 concerns convolutional networks. Its synthetic width experiment uses three-layer subnetworks and a regularized regression objective, rather than V2's two-layer teacher-student setting and extra-neuron comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors derive an equivalent convex formulation for their constrained, regularized parallel three-layer ReLU architecture and report synthetic SGD convergence improving with more subnetworks. Their polynomial-time guarantee requires fixed data rank and widths; they acknowledge exponential complexity for full-rank data and leave explicit convex representations for deeper architectures open.
record.recipe_differences: Parallel three-layer ReLU subnetworks with weight decay and squared loss; CIFAR-10 experiment uses an approximate convex formulation and plots accuracy. The paper does not test the claim's corrupted-label or near-zero classification-error conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: On the synthetic regression experiment, the reported SGD outcome changes with the number of subnetworks: small K trials tend to get stuck, while larger K allows all trials to converge to the convex-program global minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic teacher-generated regression data, small-K SGD runs tend to stop at local minima; increasing the number of parallel three-layer subnetworks allows all trials to reach the convex-program optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the number of parallel three-layer ReLU subnetworks can improve SGD convergence to the global regularized training optimum in this synthetic setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report improved accuracy and convergence from their approximate convex formulation on classification benchmarks; the supplied text does not provide readable CIFAR-10 training-accuracy endpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training an approximate convex reformulation can improve convergence and accuracy relative to training the original parallel fully connected ReLU formulation.

record.problems: CIFAR-10 training accuracy is supplied only as a plot, without textual values or a specific statement that classification training error reaches zero or near zero. The CIFAR-10 convex formulation is approximate. The explicit SGD convergence comparisons use a small synthetic regression dataset, not classification benchmarks. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the extracted outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 UCI regression training objectives and test errors are omitted because the versions concern classification-error outcomes and the listed versions do not cover regression. Figure 5 test accuracy curves are omitted because they are not training-error measurements. Figure 6 supplementary accuracy experiment is not extracted because the relevant CIFAR-10 comparison uses Adam and the text gives only a general convergence/accuracy comparison without exact values; it does not resolve whether training classification error is near zero.

untested.parts: All parts: no convolutional-network classification training-error experiment is reported.
All parts: no two-layer teacher-student width sweep or comparison adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, and initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Batch-normalization training-speed comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: CIFAR-10 alone does not establish a V1 test when the system is not convolutional. Likewise, a related overparameterization result does not establish a V2 test. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not denials of the study's reported optimization effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, Adam comparisons for classification training error, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes leaving substantial classification error are not reported as classification training-error results. CIFAR-10 training accuracy is plotted but no recoverable value is stated.

rows.subject: three-layer architecture trained with SGD, K = 2
rows.operation_detail: Five independent SGD initialization trials on synthetic regression data; compared training objective with convex-program optimum.
rows.measure: training objective value over computation time; outcomes described as getting stuck at a local minimum
rows.value: SGD trials tend to get stuck at a local minimum (text); plotted objective values are figure only
rows.note: Regression objective, not classification error. The paper explicitly describes these runs as tending to get stuck at a local minimum when K is small.
rows.check: The reported local-minimum behavior is valid for this experiment but does not measure any listed version. Three-layer parallel subnetworks and a regularized regression objective do not match V2.

rows.subject: three-layer architecture trained using the convex program
rows.operation_detail: Approximate convex program trained on CIFAR-10 using SGD; accuracy plotted over time.
rows.note: Supplementary text says the experiment verifies a performance boost from training on convex formulations, but does not state a numeric CIFAR-10 training-accuracy result.
rows.check: Remove the V1 link: this measures the proposed approximate convex formulation's performance, not the specified convolutional-network training behavior. Section A.1 gives 100 epochs for the convex formulation versus 200 for the non-convex formulation. The implemented convex objective is the penalized unconstrained formulation (16), with sampled arrangements.
